title: Offshore verification checklist and evidence playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is an operator-focused playbook for verifying that a tenant marked for offshore (non-main-region) residency is actually anchored to the expected jurisdiction. It is intended for use during onboarding, periodic audit sampling, and incident investigations.

Scope:
- Applies to private deployments and Dedicated tenancy scenarios where customers require tenant data to be processed and stored in a specific external jurisdiction.
- Covers verification for: compute placement, storage locality, network egress assertions, KMS key location, and telemetry evidence needed for external auditors.

High-level verification model (three-tier evidence):
1) Control-plane configuration evidence (declarative):
   - Tenant record showing explicit region anchor flag and pin date.
   - Deployment manifest or assignment showing node pool/zone labels (region id).
   - KMS key metadata indicating key-region and key-id (if customer-managed).
2) Runtime placement evidence (operational):
   - VM/Pod/node hostnames or host attributes demonstrating placement (zone, region).
   - Storage mount points and backing store IDs (object-store bucket region).
   - Network route / NAT gateway IDs proving no traffic egress outside region during the sampled window.
3) Behavioral evidence (telemetry & replay):
   - Ingress/egress flow logs with IPs resolved to region.
   - KV cache and prefix-hit logs showing data residency tags.
   - Short deterministic synthetic replay (test request) whose traces are captured and show strict pathing through region-local infrastructure.

Minimal acceptable evidence set (operators must gather at least one item from each tier):
- Control-plane: tenant manifest + KMS key metadata or assignment record.
- Runtime: node labels with timestamps and storage bucket location.
- Behavioral: flow logs for a 1 hour window around the check and one synthetic trace with full trace id and span list.

Checklist: onboarding / audit sampling
- [ ] Confirm customer contract clause: required jurisdiction and allowable fallback regions (if any).
- [ ] Verify tenant flag in tenancy datastore (tenant.region_anchor set -> value).
- [ ] Export deployment manifest: verify node pool label matches requested region.
- [ ] Pull KMS metadata: assert key_region == requested region or key_policy allows only that region.
- [ ] Query storage service: list buckets/volumes attached to tenant; verify region property.
- [ ] Collect last 24h flow logs for tenant-related subnets; confirm no egress IPs mapped outside region.
- [ ] Trigger synthetic replay (see 'replay procedure' below) and collect trace, spans, and logs.
- [ ] Generate evidence package (zip) with manifest, key metadata screenshot, node list, storage metadata, flow log extract, synthetic trace, operator notes, and timestamped signature.
- [ ] Create audit note in confluence and attach evidence package; include a short summary table (verification result, gaps, recommended mitigation).

Replay procedure (deterministic test request)
- Purpose: produce a reproducible, minimal request that touches all critical path components for residency (ingress, runtime, storage access, KMS call) so traces prove locality in real time.
- Steps for operator:
  1) Use the tenant's test API key (or create a short-lived test key scoped to tenant)
  2) Run command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer TEST_KEY' -d '{"prompt":"__OFFSHORE_VERIFY__"}' https://internal-request-router.local/tenants/<TENANT>/generate > /tmp/offshore_trace_resp.json
  3) Capture and export trace id from response headers: X-Trace-Id
  4) Query trace collector: curl "http://tracing.local/trace/<TRACE_ID>" -o /tmp/offshore_trace.json
  5) Verify spans: service=ingress -> service=router -> service=inference-runtime -> service=storage-client -> service=kms-client; timestamps should be within expected region-local RTT bounds.

Operator CLI snippets & expected outputs (examples)
- Tenant record: rdb-cli get-tenant --id TENANT123
  Expected: '{"id":"TENANT123","region_anchor":"eu-west-1","pin_date":"2024-09-12"}'
- Node list: infra-cli nodes --filter region=eu-west-1 --tenant TENANT123
  Expected: list of hostnames with metadata 'zone': ['eu-west-1a','eu-west-1b'] and 'owner_tenant':'TENANT123'
- Storage bucket meta: storage-cli info --bucket tenant123-eu
  Expected: 'location': 'eu-west-1', 'created_by': 'provisioner-v2'
- Flow log extract: net-cli flows --tenant TENANT123 --since 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z --until 2025-01-01T01:00:00Z | jq '.[] | select(.direction=="egress")'
  Expected: empty set or only IPs mapping to regional NATs.

Evidence packaging and signing
- Use the evidence-builder tool to collect artifacts and produce a signed bundle:
  evidence-builder collect --tenant TENANT123 --window 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z/2025-01-01T01:00:00Z --out /tmp/TENANT123-offshore-evidence.zip
- Sign the bundle with operator PGP key: gpg --sign --armor /tmp/TENANT123-offshore-evidence.zip -> TENANT123-offshore-evidence.zip.asc
- Store the signed bundle in the audit bucket (audit-retention: 10 years): aws s3 cp TENANT123-offshore-evidence.zip.asc s3://redwood-audit-offshore/TENANT123/2025-01-01/

Typical failure modes and remediation guidance
- Failure: KMS key region mismatch
  - Cause: misconfigured key alias or wrong key provisioning during onboarding.
  - Mitigation: rotate to region-correct key or reprovision key with correct region. Notify security and update tenancy manifest.
- Failure: storage bucket in wrong region
  - Cause: provisioner defaulted to global bucket naming, operator error in region param.
  - Mitigation: create new bucket in correct region, copy tenant data under customer-approved process (documented transfer), update mount metadata and decommission old bucket after confirmation.
- Failure: flow logs show transient egress via a maintenance NAT in another region
  - Cause: cross-region peering or temporary routing during maintenance window.
  - Mitigation: check routing change tickets, confirm approved maintenance window. If unapproved, escalate to network SRE and issue rollback. Record incident in audit bundle.

Escalation path (when evidence gaps remain after first pass)
- Tier 1 (operator): attempt remediation steps above and collect new evidence; annotate issues in the evidence package.
- Tier 2 (SRE/Network): open ticket PD-<auto> and include evidence bundle; request route and peering config review.
- Tier 3 (Legal/Compliance + Sales): if gap impacts contract SLA or jurisdiction commitments, schedule emergency review and notify customer success; prepare formal remediation plan and timeline.

Audit note template (one paragraph + quick table)
- Paragraph: "On <DATE> operator <NAME> performed offshore verification for tenant <TENANT>. Control-plane, runtime, and behavioral evidence were collected. Findings: PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL. Summary: <brief bullets>. Actions: <short remediation items with owners and due dates>."
- Quick table columns: check, evidence artifact path, result (pass/partial/fail), owner, due-date

Sampling cadence recommendations
- High-risk (regulated customers): weekly automated checks + full evidence package monthly.
- Medium-risk: weekly telemetry sampling + quarterly full package.
- Low-risk / dev/test tenants: monthly sampling.

Privacy and redaction guidance for audit bundles
- Redact PII before bundling (use evidence-builder --redact-pii). Keep mapping table in a separate secure store accessible only to compliance.
- For KMS metadata, do not include raw key material. Include key id and region only.

Open questions / follow-ups (for eng-private-deployments backlog)
- Should we add a deterministic header in synthetic requests to surface tenancy in traces without leaking PII? (proposal: X-Residency-Test: true)
- Investigate automating evidence-builder to push signed bundles to customer-visible secure share for self-serve proof.
- Integrate a minimal TTL notarization (timestamped hash) published to an internal audit ledger to make evidence tamper-evident.

Operator heuristics / tips
- Prefer short-lived test keys for replays to avoid contaminating production logs with long-lived test requests.
- When node labels are missing, fall back to host SNMP/metadata inventory and cross-check with cloud provider host ids.
- Keep a small curated list of 'known-good' NAT IP blocks per-region to speed flow-log validation (update quarterly).

Appendix: sample evidence manifest (CSV friendly)
artifact_type,artifact_path,notes
manifest,manifests/TENANT123-deploy.json,shows node pool region
kms_meta,screenshots/kms-tenant123-keymeta.json,contains key_id and key_region
node_list,csv/node-list-TENANT123-2025-01-01.csv,hostnames + zone labels + timestamp
flow_log,logs/flows-TENANT123-2025-01-01.jsonl,egress filter applied
trace,json/offshore-trace-TENANT123-abc123.json,tracing spans and timestamps
operator_notes,txt/ops-note-TENANT123-2025-01-01.txt,short summary and remediation items

If you use this playbook and find gap or ambiguity, please add a short note at the top of the Confluence page referenced above and assign to eng-private-deployments triage.
